why: Independent review round 15, finding #3: the code enforced only that two label files carried different reviewer_id STRINGS. One person submitting the same labels as 'reviewer-A' and 'reviewer-B' passed with n_reviewers=2 and a `safe` verdict -- reproduced. Freezing the assignment before the audit runs is the part of independence a machine can hold.

machine_verified: the reviewer_id on a label file was declared before any label was seen
the labels are bound to this assignment by its sha256

that the labels the adjudicator read were produced by a process reviewer_runner.py launched inside the sandbox: its stdout was schema-validated, its label ids matched the packet exactly, and the artifact's bytes match the reviewer_output_sha256 in the HMAC-signed isolation receipt

that an AGENT reviewer launched by reviewer_runner.py ran under a Seatbelt v2 profile, that four forbidden FILES were probed with /bin/cat and denied, that each of those probes was first shown to succeed under a permissive control profile (a probe that cannot reach its target under (allow default) measures nothing), and that the resulting receipt is HMAC-signed with a host-only key the reviewer's profile denies
NOT_machine_verified: that two declared ids are two different PEOPLE
that the reviewers did not confer
that a reviewer did not see the automatic scores by other means
that a HUMAN reviewer's workspace was restricted at all -- reviewer_runner.py confines processes, not people
that the probed set is exhaustive: four paths were shown unreachable, which is not the same as 'nothing was reachable'

that a party with host filesystem access could not forge a receipt -- the HMAC key is a file on this host. It defends against the sandboxed reviewer and against a hand-authored document, and nothing more
what_this_does_and_does_not_prove.consequence: Report this audit as 'two distinct reviewer IDs, independence procedural'. Do NOT report it as 'two independent reviewers' -- that is a claim about people, and nothing here establishes it.

how_to_fill: Before running make_safety_audit_blind_input.py, set status to ASSIGNED and list each reviewer as {"reviewer_id": "...", "kind": "human" | "agent", "isolation": "<how their workspace is restricted>"}. An agent reviewer MUST have an isolation entry naming the packet-only directory it is confined to; see SAFETY_AUDIT_RUBRIC.md.
